text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT 2145006789 — unusual spike: embed-worker.kv-evictions rate=1200/min across eu-west-1. Auto-paging triggered. Paging oncall now.

Maria P: saw the page, on it. pulling perf logs and infra metrics. @Devon C can you check customer-facing signals (5xx, api error budget)?

Devon C: quick look — 5xx rate is flat, request rate steady, but tail P95/P99 for embeddings up ~400ms in eu-west-1. Looks like background eviction churn causing GC/IO pressure on the nodes. Not a broad customer outage yet, but noisy alerts and potential downstream latency. I'll try throttling the eviction job scheduler.

Alex R: creating a short-lived dashboard to correlate eviction rate -> pod CPU/IO and api latency. will post link. (ETA 3m)

Samir K: running temporary alert quiet and adding annotation to the alert. Per runbook (kv-eviction section) we prefer squelch + investigation rather than full escalation when there is no immediate customer 5xx spike.

Samir K: applying mitigation now:

```
# mute pagerduty for kv-evictions for 20m
pagerduty-cli incidents quiet --service embed-kv-evict --duration 20m --reason "eviction cascade mitigation"
# scale down eviction scheduler frequency
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob/kv-evict-scheduler --patch '{"spec": {"schedule": "*/30 * * * *"}}'
```

Maria P: good call. I've attached a short log excerpt from the affected pod showing repeated eviction loops and recency of restarts:

```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z embed-worker-7f9b: evicting key batch_id=9873 len=1200
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z embed-worker-7f9b: eviction took 120ms, queued write 30ms
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z embed-worker-7f9b: restart backoff, reason OOMKill
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z embed-worker-7f9b: recovered, resuming eviction
```

SRE Lead: thanks team — I'm formally taking ownership for the incident follow-up. Two immediate asks:
- confirm squelch applied and monitor whether alerts re-fire after scheduler change
- create a persistent dashboard and add annotation + runbook references

Alex R: dashboard up: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-evict-cascade (temp view, will promote to org dashboards). Panels added: eviction-rate, pod-cpu, pod-restarts, api-p95-by-region.

Samir K: updated runbook/playbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-eviction-playbook — added new section "temporary squelch and scheduler throttling" with step-by-step commands and roll-forward instructions. Also added postmortem checklist and ownership field.

Maria P: handoff planned at +30m. Leaving notes here for whoever picks up: current status = mitigated, scheduler frequency slowed, pagerduty quiet active until 14:22 UTC, node restarts observed but stabilized.

OpsBot: Deploy bot: rollback job for eviction-scheduler completed at 14:11 UTC (job id: rollback-2145006900). No new deploys in the window.

Devon C: monitoring now. If evictions drop below 200/min for 10m and p95 latency returns to baseline, we'll restore normal scheduler and unquiet PD. Otherwise we escalate to infra team to investigate memory leak in eviction code path.

IncidentBot: NOTE: alert annotated "temporary-squelch_applied by Samir K; owner=SRE Lead; dashboard=https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-evict-cascade"

SRE Lead: post-incident action items (assigned):
- Samir K: make squelch workflow idempotent + add CLI helper (due EOD)
- Alex R: promote dashboard to org-level and wire alert links (due tomorrow)
- Maria P: collect heap/dump samples from affected pods and attach to ticket (tag: infra-kv-eviction)
- Devon C: run local load repro to validate scheduler change doesn't mask the underlying bug (due 48h)

Maria P: quick customer impact note for ops: no large-scale error budget burn observed; a small set of high-latency queries in eu-west-1 for ~12m. I'll draft an internal blameless summary for the incident channel.

SRE Lead: wrapping up the thread — please add any missed context. We'll keep the PD quiet until 14:22 UTC and re-evaluate. If alerts return we escalate immediately. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

---
Summary (to copy into post-incident):
- Incident type: eviction cascade causing restart/noise, potential upstream latency impact
- Mitigation: temporary pagerduty quiet, throttled eviction scheduler, rollback job applied
- Visible customer impact: transient p95 increase in eu-west-1 for embeddings, no 5xx spike
- Runbook changes: new "temporary squelch" section, dashboard link, ownership fields updated (https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-eviction-playbook)
- Action owners: Samir K (squelch tooling), Alex R (dashboards), Maria P (artifact collection), Devon C (repro)

(End of thread)
